name: Monster Trainer Monster Gambler
body:
Monster gamblers enjoy the payoff of a little risk. They challenge other trainers with their unique way of thinking that makes them unpredictable in battle.

Stack the Deck (Su)

At 1st level, before attempting an attack, saving throw, or skill check, a monster gambler can take up to a –5 penalty to that roll as a free action and grant it as a circumstance bonus to her active monster’s next attempt to perform the same action against the same target or effect. She can also use an immediate action to direct her active monster to do the same for her. This replaces eschew materials.

Take the Advantage (Ex)

The gambler gains no bonus on attacks and damage rolls against her favored enemies. Instead, she gains sneak attack, as the rogue feature. The gambler’s sneak attack damage is 1d6 at 2nd level and increases by 1d6 every 4 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 5d6 at 18th level. The gambler’s active monster can also use sneak attack, and its effective rogue level is equal to the gambler’s monster trainer level when overcoming uncanny dodge or similar abilities. At 13th level, the gambler’s sneak attack can even damage targets normally immune to precision damage. This ability alters favored enemy and replaces spell familiarity and channel monster.

Play the Odds (Ex)

At 9th level, a gambler can spend 1 use of talented trainer as a free action to reroll a single d20 before learning the outcome, but must keep the second result. She can also spend that use as an immediate action and direct her monster to do the same. This ability replaces great trainer.

Trainer Perks

The following trainer perks complement the gambler archetype: Appraise monster, evasion, fast movement, inspiring trainer, side-by-side, skilled trainer, stalwart, and uncanny dodge.
